info.title: Options Analysis Suite API
info.description:
Institutional-grade options analytics API. Programmatic access to 17 pricing models (including 7 exotic options), auto-calibration, real-time exposure analytics, WebSocket streaming, and pre-computed market data.

## Features

- **17 pricing models** — 10 standard (Black-Scholes, Heston, SABR, FFT (Carr-Madan with 6 characteristic functions), Variance Gamma, Jump Diffusion (Kou/Bates/Merton), Binomial, PDE, Monte Carlo, Local Volatility (Dupire + eSSVI)) plus 7 exotic (Barrier, Asian, Lookback, Digital, Compound, Chooser, Multi-Asset) with optional strategy-insight card via `includeInsight`
- **Auto-calibration** — Heston, SABR, VG, JD, and Local Vol calibrate against live broker chain data in 0.25-16s
- **Greek exposure** — GEX, DEX, VEX, Vanna, Charm, Vomma with gamma flip detection, call/put walls, abs gamma anchor, dealer positioning regime
- **Real-time streaming** — WebSocket endpoint for live quotes, Greeks, and computed exposure snapshots
- **Pre-computed data** — market regime, IV surfaces, snapshots, metrics, scanner, risk-neutral + lognormal probability distributions

## Authentication

All `/v1/*` endpoints require an API key. Pass it via either header:

- `Authorization: Bearer oas_live_...`
- `X-API-Key: oas_live_...`

## Rate limits

Separate buckets for data and compute endpoints (per user, shared across all API keys):

- **Data** (`/v1/data/*`): **120 requests/minute**
- **Compute** (`/v1/compute/*`): **120 requests/minute**
- **Cheap compute** (BS, binomial, exposure, max pain, expected move): max **6 concurrent**
- **Heavy compute** (MC, PDE, Heston, Local Vol, SABR, JD, VG, scenario, sensitivity): max **2 concurrent**
- **Calibration**: max **1 concurrent** job (own lane, separate from compute pools) · hard-capped at **500/day** per user
- Heavy compute endpoints may return **503** when worker capacity is unavailable
- 429 responses include `X-RateLimit-Bucket` header (`data` or `compute`)

## Broker credentials (BYOK)

Some endpoints (calibration, full-mode probability, streaming) require live broker chain data. The API doesn't pay for market data; you supply your own credentials via request headers (the streaming endpoint takes them in its initial WebSocket auth message instead):

- **TastyTrade**: `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`, `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token`, `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret`
- **Tradier**: `X-Broker-Type: tradier`, `X-Tradier-Key`
- **Schwab**: `X-Broker-Type: schwab`, `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token`, `X-Schwab-Client-Id`, `X-Schwab-Client-Secret` (calibration, full-mode probability, and streaming; streaming additionally requires a Schwab app approved for Accounts and Trading)

Note: Public.com is **not supported on the API tier** (their Individual API program restricts third-party platforms). Public is available on the Pro webapp tier for in-browser use only.

## Best practices (especially for LLM-driven agents)

- **Calibrate once, then persist the fitted params — not the `calibrationId`.** `calibrationId` is a short-lived handle into a 30-second in-memory cache; it works for immediate follow-up `/price` and `/greeks` calls but is not durable. For reuse beyond 30s, save the fitted parameters from the calibration response and pass them as `modelParams` on subsequent calls. Either path avoids the 500/day calibration quota. Don't set `resolve.calibration: true` on every repeated call for the same symbol.
- **Prefer `/v1/data/*` over recomputing.** Greeks history, IV surfaces, snapshot metrics, metrics-batch, scanner rankings, and regime classifications are precomputed or cached where available — typically much faster than recomputing from scratch. Don't loop `/v1/compute/greeks` to reconstruct what `/v1/data/greeks-history/:symbol` already returns.
- **Use batch endpoints.** `/v1/data/metrics/batch` takes multiple symbols in one call; MultiAsset accepts `modelParams.tickers` for basket pricing. One batch call beats a loop of N single-symbol calls.
- **Use canonical ticker symbols.** Symbols may contain letters, numbers, dot, dash, or slash (examples: `SPY`, `BRK.B`, `BRK-B`, `/ES`). Space-separated class shares such as `BRK B` are rejected; use dot or dash form instead.
- **Use ticker auto-fill instead of fabricated numerics.** Pass `symbol` + `expiry` and let the API resolve `S`, `sigma`, `r`, `t` from cached market data — the response's `resolved` block shows which source filled each field (`snapshot`, `atmIv-expiry`, `hv-20d`, `fred-DGS3MO`, …). Don't hallucinate market values from training data.
- **Always inspect `warnings` and `resolved`.** The compute route returns top-level `warnings` plus a `resolved` block whenever ticker auto-fill ran. Agents that ignore these can act on a price computed with a stale spot or a missing-dividend fallback.
- **Honor `Retry-After` on 429.** Sleep the suggested duration. Retrying instantly in a tight loop wastes tokens and bounces off the same limit.
- **Use `X-Cache-Status` to guide polling cadence.** Data responses include `X-Cache-Status`; values include `HIT`, `MISS`, `DEDUP`, `NO_REDIS`, and error/fallback statuses. If you see all HITs, you're polling faster than the underlying data updates — back off.
- **Don't repoll faster than the underlying data updates.** Most `/v1/data/*` endpoints back tables that refresh on a documented daily cron. Repolling every 30s returns the same bytes.
- **Stream live data over `/v1/ws`, don't poll REST.** Up to 30 msg/sec × 50 symbols × 5 sessions beats any REST polling loop on freshness and rpm budget.
- **Match model to task.** Black-Scholes and Binomial are sub-100ms and correct for vanilla options. Reserve Heston/SABR/Local Vol/JD/MC for cases where skew, jumps, or path-dependence actually matter.
- **Scope and secure keys.** Create compute-only, data-only, or streaming-only keys to limit blast radius. Never embed keys in client-side JS, browser extensions, public repos, or LLM tool manifests.

post.description:
Price an option using one of 17 supported pricing models. For advanced models, pass model-specific parameters via `modelParams`, or use a `calibrationId` from `/v1/compute/calibrate` to reuse calibrated parameters.

**Required tenor:** every request must specify a time-to-expiry. Provide either `t` (numeric years) **or** `expiry` / `expiration` (YYYY-MM-DD). Missing both returns a `400` validation error.

**Ticker auto-fill:** supply `symbol: "AAPL"` (plus `expiry: "YYYY-MM-DD"` since tenor is mandatory) to let the API fill `S`, `sigma`, `q`, `r`, and `t` from cached market data. User-supplied numeric fields always win; the response `resolved` block reports the effective value + source (`override`, `snapshot`, `atmIv-expiry`, `hv-20d`, `ratios_ttm`, `profile_yield`, `fred-DGS3MO`, etc.). For MultiAsset, supply `modelParams.tickers: ["SPY","QQQ",...]` to build the basket from 5y monthly correlations. Requires both `compute` and `data` scopes on the API key. Set `resolve.calibration: true` (Heston/SABR/VG/JD/LocalVol only) to additionally run auto-calibration under the existing calibration quota — broker headers (`X-Broker-Type`, `X-Tradier-Key`, …) are required for this mode.

**modelParams by model:**

- **heston:** `v0` / `initialVariance` / `hestonV0`, `kappa` / `hestonKappa`, `theta` / `hestonTheta`, `volOfVol` / `sigmaV` / `hestonXi` / `xi` / `hestonVolOfVol` (legacy alias: `sigma`), `rho` / `hestonRho`, `integrationPoints` (legacy alias: `hestonOrder`). Every spelling listed here is accepted identically on `/price`, `/greeks` and `/sensitivity`. Omitted parameters take these defaults, which materially affect the price: `v0` = `sigma^2`, `theta` = `sigma^2`, `kappa` = 2.0, `volOfVol` = 0.3, `rho` = -0.7, `integrationPoints` = 16. Supply them explicitly (or via a calibration) rather than relying on the defaults. Domain rules, applied identically on `/price`, `/greeks` and `/sensitivity` and rejected with a 422 `INVALID_HESTON_PARAMS`: `v0 >= 0`, `theta >= 0` (both are variances), `kappa > 0` (a mean-reversion speed), `volOfVol >= 0`, and `-1 < rho < 1` strictly. Every one of these parameters must be a number or a numeric string; booleans, arrays and objects are rejected with a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` rather than coerced. `integrationPoints` is the exception to the last rule only in range: a value outside 8..128 is clamped into it rather than rejected. Where a canonical spelling and a legacy alias are both supplied, the canonical one wins (`volOfVol` over `sigma`, `integrationPoints` over `hestonOrder`). On `/v1/compute/greeks`, the volatility Greeks (`vega`, `vomma`, `vanna`, `veta`, `zomma`, `ultima`, `dcharmDvol`) are taken with respect to the model`s own instantaneous volatility `sqrt(v0)`, not the request `sigma`. With `v0` omitted the two coincide, since `v0` then defaults to `sigma^2`. Note that `sigma` stops influencing the Heston price only once BOTH `v0` and `theta` are supplied - supplying `v0` alone leaves `theta` defaulting to `sigma^2`, so `sigma` still moves the price through the long-run variance (with `v0` = 0.09 and `theta` omitted, `sigma` of 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 prices 9.4410 / 10.8481 / 15.0780).
- **sabr:** `sabrAlpha` / `alpha`, `sabrBeta` / `beta`, `sabrRho` / `rho`, `sabrNu` / `nu`, `approximationMethod` (hagan | obloj | paulot, default hagan), `shift`, `expansionOrder`, `useSmallTimeCorrection`, `fixBeta`, `fixedBetaValue`, `atmReference`, `volFloor`, `useArbitrageChecks`
- **fft:** `processType` (blackScholes | merton | varianceGamma | heston | kou | bates), `N`, `alpha`, `eta`, `integrationMethod` (legacy aliases: `fftGridSize`, `fftAlpha`, `fftEta`, `fftIntegrationMethod`). Process-specific params match the webapp: Merton `mertonLambda`, `mertonMuJ`, `mertonSigmaJ`; Variance Gamma `vgSigma`, `vgNu`, `vgTheta`; Heston `hestonV0`, `hestonKappa`, `hestonTheta`, `hestonXi`, `hestonRho`; Kou `kouLambda`, `kouP`, `kouEta1`, `kouEta2`; Bates `batesV0`, `batesKappa`, `batesTheta`, `batesSigmaV`, `batesRho`, `batesLambda`, `batesMuJ`, `batesSigmaJ`
- **vg:** `sigma` / `vgSigma`, `nu` / `vgNu`, `theta` / `vgTheta`, optional `method`, `fftPoints`, `alpha`, `eta`, `cacheFFT`, `weighting`
- **jd:** `modelType` / `jdModel` (kou | merton | bates, default kou; any other value is rejected with a 422 rather than falling back to kou). Merton/Kou accept `baseVolatility` as the diffusion sigma override. Kou: `lambda`, `pUp`, `etaUp`, `etaDown`, optional `tailTolerance` / `tailTol`, `maxK`, `forceFFT`, `fftGridSize`. Merton: `lambda`, `muJ`, `sigmaJ`, optional `maxPoisson`. Bates: `v0`, `kappa`, `theta`, `sigmaV` / `volOfVol` / `xi`, `rho`, `lambda`, `muJ`, `sigmaJ`, optional `forceExactCF`, `fftGridSize`. Jump defaults when omitted: `lambda` = 0.1, `muJ` = -0.05, `sigmaJ` = 0.15, `pUp` = 0.5, `etaUp` = `etaDown` = 10, `maxK` = 30.
- **binomial:** `steps`, `enableAmerican` / `isAmerican`, `treeType` (CRR | JR | LR, default LR), optional Richardson controls `useRichardsonExtrap`, `richardsonMode`, `stepMultiplier`, `extrapOrder`, and discrete-dividend inputs either as `dividends` array or the webapp-style `useDiscreteDividends`, `exDividendDates`, `dividendAmounts`. The public API uses the ex-date discrete-dividend model. `steps` and `enableAmerican` / `isAmerican` are also accepted as top-level request fields; where both are supplied the `modelParams` spelling wins, because the generated SDKs populate the top-level pair with their own defaults even when the caller never set them. `treeType` selects the lattice construction: `CRR` is Cox-Ross-Rubinstein; `JR` keeps equal-magnitude CRR up/down factors (`u·d = 1`) and puts drift into the risk-neutral probability (this is NOT the equal-probability Jarrow-Rudd 1983 tree, which puts drift into `u`/`d` with `p = 1/2` and breaks finite-difference cross-Greeks because `u·d ≠ 1`); `LR` is Leisen-Reimer with Peizer-Pratt inversion method 2, is the DEFAULT when `treeType` is omitted, and rounds an even `steps` UP to the next odd count, except at the public 2000-step ceiling where up is unavailable so it rounds DOWN to 1999 (same rule the engine applies at its own higher MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS). `exDividendDates` entries may be given in YEARS or in DAYS to the ex-date, and a bare number cannot say which - `2.5` on a 3-year option is a legitimate 2.5 days and a legitimate 2.5 years, and the two price differently. Set `dividendTimeUnit` (alias `exDividendTimeUnit`) to `days` or `years` to say which; any other value is rejected with a 422. When it is omitted the legacy rule applies unchanged: entries greater than 2 are read as DAYS, entries of 2 or less as YEARS. Under either reading, an entry that falls after expiry is dropped because it cannot affect the price. Greek accuracy, on the default `LR`: `delta`, `vega`, `rho`, `vanna`, `vomma` and `ultima` match Black-Scholes to better than 0.05% at the money, and `theta`, `charm`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` to better than 0.15%. `gamma` converges from 1.13% at 50 steps to 0.04% at 1600. `speed`, `zomma` and `color` are the loosest, measured 28.4%, 6.7% and 7.0% at 50 steps, 7.7%, 1.5% and 1.6% at the default 200, and 0.96%, -0.02% and 0.01% at 1600; raise `steps` when the third-order Greeks matter. Away from the money the worst of the seventeen at 200 steps is `zomma` at 20.4%, then `speed` at 9.2% and `color` at 8.9%, with everything else inside 1.2%. Accuracy degrades at low volatility, where these Greeks are also small in absolute terms.

  **`CRR` publishes accurate prices and first-order Greeks, but its higher-order Greeks are only meaningful when `S = K`.** Cox-Ross-Rubinstein centres its lattice on SPOT with `u·d = 1`, so a node lands on the strike only at the money; anywhere else, each bumped reprice moves the payoff kink between nodes and the finite differences measure that motion rather than the option. In practice the CRR cross-Greeks return approximately the at-the-money value at every spot - at K=100, sigma=0.2, 200 steps, `vanna` reads about -0.095 whether the true value is +1.43 (S=80) or -0.96 (S=120). Worst-case error over S in {80, 90, 110, 120}: `vanna` 110%, `charm` 145%, `vomma` 212%, `veta` 55%, `speed` 23%, `zomma` 148%, `ultima` 200%, `dcharmDvol` 218%. This is structural rather than a resolution limit - the same errors appear at 800 steps - and it begins immediately, at 18% for `vanna` by 0.2% moneyness and 50% by 1%, so there is no tolerance band inside which CRR higher-order Greeks can be trusted off the money. `CRR` price, `delta`, `gamma`, `vega`, `theta`, `rho`, `epsilon`, `phi` and `lambda` are unaffected and remain accurate. Use the default `LR` for any Greek above first order; `CRR` is retained because it is the canonical textbook construction that callers cross-check against. `JR` shares the same `u·d = 1` geometry as `CRR` and therefore the same limitation.
- **pde:** `forceMethod` / `pdeForceMethod` (`analytical` | `pde` | `pde-with-fallback`, normalized case-insensitively; unsupported values return 422), `accuracyThreshold` / `pdeAccuracyThreshold` (non-negative; malformed or negative values return 422), plus grid controls `spaceSteps`, `timeSteps`, `sMin`, `sMax`, `gridSpacing`, `rannacherSteps`
- **mc:** `paths` / `mcPaths` / `nPaths`, `steps` / `stepsPerPath` / `timeSteps` / `nSteps`, `seed` / `mcSeed`, `process` / `processType` (`blackscholes` | `jumpdiffusion` | `meanreverting` | `heston` | `localvolcev` | `localvoldupire`; aliases such as `BlackScholes`, `Merton`, `LocalVolatility`, `Dupire`, and `CEV` are normalized), top-level process params or nested `processParams`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`, `useImportanceSampling`, `useMomentMatching`, `useQMC`, `qmcType` (`sobol` | `halton`; other values return 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM`). `processType`, `qmcType`, and `rngMethod` must be strings when supplied; arrays, booleans, and objects return 422 rather than being string-coerced. `rngMethod: SobolTrue` is normalized to Sobol QMC; non-QMC browser RNG labels fall back to the standard server RNG path. Monte Carlo pricing in the API is European-only. Browser-only execution flags such as `useGPU`, `batchSize`, and `parallelThreads` are ignored server-side. Nested `processParams` may supply process-specific fields but cannot override the validated request coordinates `S`, `r`, `q`, `sigma`, or `T`. QMC dimension is the path step count: Sobol supports at most 40 `nSteps` and Halton at most 10. A larger value (including the 252-step non-GBM default when `nSteps` is omitted) returns a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` rather than silently running the pseudo-random path or surfacing a generator error.

  `seed` / `mcSeed` is validated rather than coerced: it must be an integer with `|seed| < 2^52` and must not be 0. Zero is rejected because the engine builds its generator with `seed || Date.now()`, so a zero seed silently becomes the wall clock - and on `/v1/compute/greeks` the seed is reused across every bumped evaluation to give common random numbers, so a wall-clock seed would make each bump draw a different stream and the Greeks would measure Monte Carlo noise rather than the bump. Fractional, out-of-range, non-numeric and array/boolean/object values return a `422` with `code: "INVALID_MODEL_PARAM"`; a numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer (`"1337"` yes, `"1.5"` no). On the standard pseudo-random path the generator reduces the seed to 32 bits, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. That equivalence does NOT extend to the QMC paths (`useQMC` with Sobol or Halton): those initializers scale the raw seed before reducing it, and above 2^53 / 1664525 the multiply loses precision, so two seeds a multiple of 2^32 apart diverge - seeds 1 and 1 + 1000x2^32 price 10.6572 vs 10.4724 under Sobol and 10.5099 vs 11.4230 under Halton, against an identical 9.0366 on the standard path. Repeating the same seed is deterministic on every path, and on every supported `processType`. With a valid seed, repeating a request returns the identical price.
  Two of the six processes carry their own instantaneous-volatility input: `heston` reads `v0` (the instantaneous variance, aliased `hestonV0`; where both spellings are present `hestonV0` wins, matching the process itself) and `meanreverting` reads `meanRevertSigma`. Either may be a number or a non-blank numeric string; accepted strings are normalized before pricing so `/price` and `/greeks` use the same value. Supplied non-numeric, blank, or negative values return a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` on both endpoints rather than being quietly replaced. Heston permits the valid boundary `v0 = 0`; mean-reverting requires `meanRevertSigma > 0` because its engine treats zero as omission. A request-level `sigma = 0` is likewise preserved rather than defaulted to 0.2, and omitted Heston `v0` / `theta` then derive as zero. Explicit Heston `theta = 0` and `sigmaV = 0` are also preserved rather than replaced by their defaults.
  On `/v1/compute/greeks`, the volatility Greeks (`vega`, `vanna`, `vomma`, `veta`, `zomma`, `ultima`, `dcharmDvol`) are differentiated with respect to whichever state the process actually reads: `sqrt(v0)` for Heston (matching the semi-analytic `heston` model), `meanRevertSigma` for mean-reverting, and the request `sigma` for every other process. With explicit Heston `v0`, only that state moves and request `sigma` stays fixed, so an omitted long-run variance `theta` remains at the value `/price` derived from request `sigma`. With `v0` omitted, the stencil rewrites its implicit `v0 = sigma^2`; an implicit `theta = sigma^2` moves with it, preserving the pre-existing derivative coordinate. The scaled step keeps ordinary positive values in range. At `v0 = 0`, and at request `sigma = 0` for the five generic-volatility processes, the centered stencil uses the even continuation in volatility rather than sending a negative magnitude to the engine. A positive value so small that the second- or third-order finite-difference denominator underflows can still be priced, but `/greeks` returns a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` instead of publishing sanitized zero derivatives.
- **localvol:** PDE-only public surface. Supported params: `impliedVolData` (array or JSON string), `impliedVolDataArray`, `useDupire`, `useAmerican`, `interpolation` (essvi | linear | svi | dupire; cubic is no longer supported), `spotSteps` / `pdeGridSize`, `timeSteps` / `pdeTimeSteps`, `rannacherSteps`, `regularizationParam`, `localVolBeta` / `beta` / `cevBeta`, `cevScale`, `minVol` / `dupireMinVol`, `maxVol` / `dupireMaxVol`, `ticker`
- **barrier:** `barrierType` (up-out | down-out | up-in | down-in | double-out | double-in), `barrierLevel`, `rebate`, `monitoringType` (continuous | discrete | window), `monitoringFreq`, `upperBarrier`, `lowerBarrier`, `upperRebate`, `lowerRebate`, `windowStart`, `windowEnd`
- **asian:** `averagingType` (arithmetic | geometric), `strikeType` (fixed | floating), `method` (curran | geometric; `mc`/`montecarlo` requests are normalized to curran server-side), `numObservations` (omitted and zero use the pricer's `floor(252 * t)` default - `ASIAN_DEFAULTS` carries `0`, so zero does not mean "one fixing"; positive values truncate toward zero, a result below 1 retains the zero/default behavior, and the effective count clamps to 1..2048; negative, non-finite, empty, boolean, array and object values return 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM`), `observationFreq`, `observationDates` (array or JSON-encoded array of future times to each fixing in years from the valuation time; it must contain at least one date, and dates must be finite, positive, strictly increasing and no later than `t`; malformed/non-array/empty values, violations of those rules, and schedules over 2048 entries return 422 rather than silently using or truncating the generated schedule. On `/greeks`, elapsed finite-difference time is subtracted from every date, explicit or derived, preserving the calendar spacing; the step is shortened when needed so it cannot pass the first fixing. An omitted schedule is materialized once at the requested tenor and then shifted the same way, so the time Greeks measure the decay of the position held rather than a family of contracts re-specified at each bumped tenor; this can change time Greeks materially compared with the old rescaled-schedule behavior. `observationDates` now also applies to `averagingType: "arithmetic"`, which previously derived its schedule from `(t, numObservations)` alone and ignored the parameter; where a schedule is supplied its length defines the future fixing count, matching the geometric path), `pastFixings`, `runningAverage`, `runningSum`, `fixingsElapsed`. `fixingDates` and `observations` are accepted aliases for the observation COUNT, not for a schedule; passing an array to either returns 422
- **lookback:** `lookbackType` (floating | fixed), `currentMax`, `currentMin`, `monitoringType` / `monitoring`, `monitoringFrequency`, `method`
- **digital:** `type` / `digitalType` — accepts either short form (`cash` | `asset` | `gap`) or long form (`cash-or-nothing` | `asset-or-nothing` | `gap`); both are equivalent server-side. Also `cashAmount`, `gapAmount`, `smoothing` (clamped server-side to a minimum of 1e-4), `method`
- **compound:** `compoundType` (call-on-call | call-on-put | put-on-call | put-on-put), `underlyingStrike`, `firstExpiry`, `secondExpiry` (defaults to request `t`), `method`, `mcPaths`, `mcSeed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`. Requires 0 < `firstExpiry` < `secondExpiry`; violations are rejected with a 422 on both `/price` and `/greeks`. A supplied `mcPaths` is clamped to 2..1000000; when it is omitted the pricer applies its own default of **10000** paths, so omitting it is not the same as sending 100000. The lower bound is 2 rather than 1 because the antithetic path pairs `floor(mcPaths / 2)` draws, and a single path yields none. `mcSeed` does not clamp: it must be an integer with `|mcSeed| < 2^52` and must not be 0 (the pricer reads `mcSeed || Date.now()`, so a zero seed would silently become the wall clock). Fractional, out-of-range, non-numeric and array/boolean/object values are rejected with a 422. A numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer: `"1337"` yes, `"1.0000000000000001"` no. Two limits worth knowing rather than discovering. First, the seed is reduced to 32 bits by the generator, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. Second, a JSON number literal is rounded to a double by the parser before the API ever sees it, so a fraction finer than the double spacing at your magnitude is already gone and no server-side check can recover it - `1.0000000000000001` arrives as `1`. That is why seeds at or above 2^52 are refused outright (there the spacing reaches 1, so any fractional literal has already become an integer), and why the string form is the exact one at every magnitude.
- **chooser:** `chooserType` (simple | complex; anything else is a 422), `choiceTime`, `maturity`, `callStrike`, `putStrike`, `callMaturity`, `putMaturity`, `method`, `mcPaths`, `rngSeed` / `seed` / `mcSeed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`. `choiceTime` must be positive. A **simple** chooser additionally requires `maturity` > `choiceTime`; a **complex** chooser requires `callMaturity` > `choiceTime` and `putMaturity` > `choiceTime` (`maturity` only supplies their default). Violations are rejected with a 422 on both `/price` and `/greeks`. A supplied `mcPaths` is clamped to 2..1000000, but note the effective floor is higher: the chooser pricer runs `max(mcPaths, 20000)` paths, so any value below 20000 - including the 10000 it defaults to when omitted - executes at 20000. Monte Carlo pricing is deterministic: `rngSeed` (also accepted as `seed` or `mcSeed`) defaults to 1337, and repeating a request returns the same price. It must be an integer with `|seed| < 2^52`; fractional, non-numeric, and array/boolean/object values return a 422, and a numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer (`"1337"` yes, `"1.5"` no). Unlike `mc`, `compound` and `multiasset`, a seed of **0 is accepted** here: this engine tests for `undefined`/`null` rather than falsiness and its Mulberry32 generator adds a constant before first use, so state 0 is a working stream rather than a silent fallback to the wall clock. The generator reduces the seed with `seed >>> 0`, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. On `/v1/compute/greeks` the seed is reused across every bumped evaluation and the same resolved seed is used by the optional insight repricer, so both remain deterministic and the Greeks measure the bump rather than sampling noise.
- **multiasset:** `payoffType` / `type` / `multiAssetType` (basket | spread | max | min), `numAssets`, `correlation`, `corrMatrix` / `correlationMatrix`, `prices[]`, `volatilities[]`, `dividends[]`, `weights[]`, `method`, `mcPaths`, `seed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`, `useSobol`. If `prices[]` is omitted, the request spot `S` is used as the first asset price. Monte Carlo pricing is deterministic: `seed` defaults to 1337, and repeating a request returns the same price. `seed` must be an integer whose unsigned 32-bit value is non-zero - the generator is seeded with `seed >>> 0`, so 0 and any multiple of 2^32 are rejected with a 422, as are non-integer, non-numeric, and out-of-range values at or above 2^52. A numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer: `"1337"` yes, `"1.0000000000000001"` no. One limit no server-side check can close: a JSON number literal is rounded to a double by the parser before it reaches the API, so a fraction finer than the double spacing at your magnitude is already gone - `1.0000000000000001` arrives as `1`. That is why the 2^52 bound exists (at and above it the spacing reaches 1, so a fractional literal has already become an integer) and why the string form is the exact one at every magnitude. The remaining numeric knobs do normalize rather than reject: `mcPaths` is clamped to 1..1000000 and defaults to 100000. `numAssets` resolves to the LARGEST of the explicit value (truncated toward zero, or 2 when omitted) and the lengths of any supplied `prices[]` / `volatilities[]` / `dividends[]` / `weights[]`, capped at 32 - so `numAssets: 2` with three prices resolves to three assets, and an omitted count with a single price still resolves to two. Each of those arrays is then padded or truncated to the resolved count using the request `S` / `sigma` / `q` and equal weights.

post.description:
Price a multi-leg options strategy in a single call and get its net cost, position-level net Greeks, risk metrics (max profit/loss, breakevens, profit zone, risk/reward, probability of profit), and a payoff-at-expiry curve.

Each option leg is priced through the same model dispatcher as `/v1/compute/price` and `/v1/compute/greeks` — set a per-leg `model` of `bs` (European) or `binomial` (American-aware, with `isAmerican`, `steps`, and a discrete-dividend schedule in `modelParams`). Supply `premium` on a leg to value it at an observed market premium instead of the model price; omit it to use the model. Stock legs use `costBasis` (per share, defaults to the shared spot) and `quantity` in shares.

Legs share the underlying `S`/`r`/`q` and, by default, `sigma`/`t`; a leg may override `sigma` and `t` for a skew or a diagonal. Net Greeks are share-equivalent: an option leg contributes `signedQty x 100 x per-contract Greek`, a stock leg contributes `signedQty` to delta, and short legs are negative — so a covered call (100 long shares, 1 short call) nets a positive but sub-100 delta. Unbounded max profit/loss are returned as null with `unbounded` flags, since JSON cannot carry Infinity.

post.description:
Compute the implied probability distribution of the underlying at expiration. Returns BOTH the risk-neutral distribution (eSSVI + Breeden-Litzenberger with finite-difference fallback) AND a lognormal baseline, plus statistics (implied move, range bounds, fair value). Supports two modes:

- **simple**: Pre-computed strikes + IVs (no broker needed)
- **full**: BYOK broker credentials; API fetches live chain across multiple expirations and calibrates eSSVI

### Data requirements

At least **5 strikes** are required. The Breeden-Litzenberger second difference is taken on interior points only, so N strikes yield N-2 density points and the extractor needs 3 of them. The public request validator returns 400 for fewer than 5; broker chains that prepare fewer than 5 usable strikes return 422 `INSUFFICIENT_DISTRIBUTION_DATA`.

In `mode: "simple"`, every strike must carry a positive `iv`; an unusable value is rejected rather than substituted, because that strike's call price feeds the second difference and would bend the whole published density. In `mode: "full"`, an `expiration` that is not listed for the symbol returns a 422 `UNKNOWN_EXPIRATION` rather than being silently swapped for the front month; a listed expiration after its 4:00 p.m. `America/New_York` close returns 422 `EXPIRED_EXPIRATION` rather than being repriced at a one-day floor.

When the density cannot be extracted, `riskNeutral.pdf` is empty, `riskNeutral.stats` is `null`, and `riskNeutral.fallbackReason` carries the reason. `lognormal.stats` is `null` when the chain has no usable implied volatilities to average.

### Required headers for `mode: "full"`

- **Tradier** (1 credential header) — uses a static Production Access Token:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tradier`
  - `X-Tradier-Key: <your Tradier production access token>`
- **Tastytrade** (2 credential headers) — uses OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow. The server posts `{grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token, client_secret}` to Tastytrade's token endpoint to mint a short-lived access token, which is reused until near expiry. Both values must come from the **same Tastytrade OAuth app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token: <OAuth refresh token from your Tastytrade OAuth app>`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret: <OAuth client secret from the SAME Tastytrade OAuth app>`
- **Schwab** (3 credential headers) — per-user-app OAuth 2.0 (BYOK). Register your own Schwab app and bring its `client_id` + `client_secret` plus a `refresh_token` from the Schwab OAuth redirect. The server exchanges them (HTTP Basic auth) for a ~30-minute access token, reused until near expiry. All three must come from the **same Schwab app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: schwab`
  - `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token: <refresh token from your Schwab OAuth app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Id: <client id of the SAME Schwab app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Secret: <client secret of the SAME Schwab app>`

`mode: "simple"` requires no headers. Public.com is not supported on the API tier.

Credential sources: Tradier → https://docs.tradier.com/docs/getting-started · Tastytrade → https://developer.tastytrade.com/oauth/ · Schwab → https://developer.schwab.com/

post.description:
Fetches the live options chain from the specified broker (BYOK credentials via headers) and calibrates model parameters. Returns fitted parameters + calibration ID for reuse in `/price` and `/greeks` via the `calibrationId` field. Supports Heston, SABR, VG, JD, and Local Volatility (eSSVI multi-expiration surface).

### Required headers by broker

- **Tradier** (1 credential header) — uses a static Production Access Token:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tradier`
  - `X-Tradier-Key: <your Tradier production access token>`
- **Tastytrade** (2 credential headers) — uses OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow. The server posts `{grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token, client_secret}` to `https://api.tastyworks.com/oauth/token` to mint a short-lived access token, which is reused until near expiry; separately, calibration results themselves are cached for 30 seconds. Both credential values must come from the **same Tastytrade OAuth app** — the `client_secret` identifies which app issued the refresh token, so dropping either header fails the OAuth exchange:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token: <OAuth refresh token from your Tastytrade OAuth app>`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret: <OAuth client secret from the SAME Tastytrade OAuth app>`
- **Schwab** (3 credential headers) — per-user-app OAuth 2.0 (BYOK). The server posts `grant_type=refresh_token` with HTTP Basic auth over `client_id:client_secret` to `https://api.schwabapi.com/v1/oauth/token` to mint a ~30-minute access token, reused until near expiry. All three values must come from the **same Schwab app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: schwab`
  - `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token: <refresh token from your Schwab OAuth app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Id: <client id of the SAME Schwab app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Secret: <client secret of the SAME Schwab app>`

Public.com is not supported on the API tier (their Individual API program restricts third-party platforms). Web-app Pro users can still use Public directly in the browser.

**Market assumptions:** Supply `riskFreeRate` and `dividendYield`, or let the API resolve them from stored rate/dividend data. If either remains unresolved, the public endpoint returns 422 `RESOLUTION_FAILED`; it never substitutes `0.05` or `0`. A value that is SUPPLIED but not a number or a numeric string returns 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` naming the spelling you used, rather than being coerced - `true` and `""` used to calibrate at a 100% and a 0% rate respectively. The resolved assumptions are included in the short-lived calibration cache key.

**Failure semantics:** A chain with too few usable observations returns 422 `INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_DATA`. A calibrator that reports fallback/default parameters, an explicit error, or no finite non-negative fit metric returns 422 `CALIBRATION_FAILED`; those parameters are not cached or returned with a fabricated zero RMSE. Upstream broker failures remain server errors rather than being relabelled as caller input defects.

**Quotas:** Calibrations are hard-capped at **500 per day** per user (in addition to the 120/min compute rate limit). Over-quota returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header and a `CalibrationQuotaError` body. The quota window resets at midnight UTC. Cached calibration responses (30-second TTL per `credentials.type + symbol + model + expiration + modelParams + market assumptions` key) still count against the quota.

get.description:
Quarterly earnings history, EPS and revenue surprises, and next earnings date. Sourced from `earnings_data` table.

**Options analytics (`?includeOptionsAnalytics=true`)** — attach an `optionsAnalytics` block containing realized vs implied post-earnings moves, IV crush, and aggregate stats across the last 8 quarters. Derived by joining the earnings history with `stock_prices` (close-to-close realized move) and `scan_tickers` (historical ATM IV, tenor preference 7D → 30D → generic). Adds ~2 extra database reads; the base response is unchanged when the flag is false or absent.

**Windowing:** BMO (before-open) reports use prior-day close → report-day close. AMC or unknown-timing reports use report-day close → next-trading-day close. The response `quarters[].time` echoes the source `time` tag when available (currently often `null`, which falls through to AMC-style windowing).

**`impliedMovePct`** is a 1-trading-day approximation: `preEventAtmIv × √(1/252) × 100`. Event vol concentrates in the event-week expiration, so this often understates what options actually priced in; use it as a lower bound. `realizedOverImplied > 1` means the stock moved more than options priced in. `ivCrushPct` is `(preIv − postIv) / preIv × 100`.

parameters.name: includeOptionsAnalytics
parameters.description: When `true`, attach `optionsAnalytics` with per-quarter realized/implied move, IV crush, and aggregate stats (last 8 reported quarters).

upPct.description: Share of quarters with non-negative close-to-close move.

time.description: Report timing if the source tagged it; unknown/unrecognized values are normalized to null (falls through to AMC-style windowing).

preEventAtmIv.description: Decimal IV at pre-event close (e.g. 0.42 for 42%).

ivTenorUsed.description: Which IV tenor satisfied the pre-event lookup.

ivCrushTenorUsed.description: The single fixed-maturity tenor BOTH legs of `ivCrushPct` were read from. May differ from `ivTenorUsed`: the pre- and post-event rows are each resolved at their own best tenor for `preEventAtmIv`/`impliedMovePct`, but the crush requires one tenor present in both. Deliberately excludes `generic`, which is a `30d ?? 7d ?? nearest` fallback rather than a fixed maturity, so two rows carrying it may still be different tenors. Null when the rows share no fixed tenor, in which case `ivCrushPct` is null rather than comparing across maturities.

ivCrushPreIv.description: Pre-event IV at `ivCrushTenorUsed` — the exact left-hand input to `ivCrushPct`. Reported separately from `preEventAtmIv`, which may sit at a different tenor.

ivCrushPostIv.description: Post-event IV at `ivCrushTenorUsed` — the exact right-hand input to `ivCrushPct`.

ivCrushPct.description: Positive = vol collapsed (crush). Computed as (ivCrushPreIv - ivCrushPostIv) / ivCrushPreIv × 100, both legs at `ivCrushTenorUsed` — NOT from preEventAtmIv/postEventAtmIv, which may sit at different tenors.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices, including ticker-resolution warnings and disclosure that a requested numerical model used an analytical fallback.

ciHigh.description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the price.

nPaths.description: Effective number of paths the estimate was built from. With antithetic variates enabled this is up to 2× the requested `nPaths`.

McDistribution.description: Terminal underlying-price distribution from a Monte Carlo simulation. Present only when `model: "mc"` and `detail: "distribution"` (or `"full"`). Computed from every simulated path — does not subsample.

mean.description: Mean of the simulated terminal price.

topStrikes.description: Top-10 strikes by absolute net gamma

ExposureFullResult.description: Full result: compact snapshot plus the entire by-strike Greek-exposure array.

ExposureResponse.description: Default: ExposureFullResult ({ snapshot, byStrike }). With ?detail=snapshot: ExposureSnapshot directly.

ScenarioMatrixEntry.description: One cell in the scenario matrix: option value and P/L at a spot and volatility perturbation.

spot.description: Scenario spot price after applying spotChange.

pnl.description: Dollar P/L versus the base option price.

pnlPercent.description: Percent P/L versus the base option price.

model.description: Model used for the matrix. `bs` (European Black-Scholes) unless `model: "binomial"` was requested.

matrix.description: 2D matrix of structured cells indexed by [spotChange][volChange].

SensitivityResponse.description: Per-axis sweep of Greeks. Each point carries the full 17-Greek set under Black-Scholes (model defaults to "bs"). When `model: "heston"`, points additionally carry a `modelGreeks` block with derivatives w.r.t. the Heston parameters (V0, kappa, theta, volOfVol, rho). When `model: "binomial"`, each point carries `price`, `delta`, and `gamma` only.

SensitivityPoint.description: One point on a sensitivity sweep. `x` is the sweep variable (spot price for axis="spot", days-to-expiry for "time", volatility for "volatility"). The standard 17 Greeks come from Black-Scholes; `modelGreeks` is present only when `model: "heston"`. Under `model: "binomial"` only `price`, `delta`, and `gamma` are populated.

x.description: Sweep variable value at this point.

HestonModelGreeks.description: Sensitivities of the Heston price to its five model parameters. Present only when `model: "heston"` was requested. Computed by symmetric finite-difference around the calibrated parameter point; useful for assessing exposure to a miscalibrated Heston model (vs. classic Greeks which assume the model is correct and only the market inputs vary).

dV0.description: d(price) / d(V0) — sensitivity to instantaneous variance.

StrategyLeg.description: One priced leg of the strategy. Option legs carry `strike`, `model`, and `premium` (per share); stock legs carry `costBasis` (per share). `greeks` are per-contract for options and `{ delta: 1 }` for stock.

premium.description: Per-share option premium used — supplied by the caller or computed by the model.

costBasis.description: Per-share cost basis for a stock leg (defaults to the shared spot).

greeks.description: Per-contract Greeks for option legs; `{ delta: 1 }` for stock.

type.description: One of: above, below, between, outside, always_profit, always_loss, complex, unknown.

profitIntervals.description: Profitable price bands [lo, hi] for disjoint (complex) zones. A null endpoint means unbounded on that side (0 low / +inf high).

payoff.description: Total P&L at expiry at this price (intrinsic payoff plus the initial cost).

StrategyResponse.description: Net cost, position-level net Greeks, risk metrics, and a payoff-at-expiry curve for a multi-leg strategy. Unbounded profit/loss and an unbounded risk/reward ratio are reported as null (JSON has no Infinity); the `unbounded` flags say which.

initialCost.description: Net cash flow to establish the position: negative = net debit paid, positive = net credit received. Options are x100/contract; stock is x shares.

netGreeks.description: Position-level (share-equivalent) net Greeks: an option leg contributes signedQty x 100 x per-contract Greek; a stock leg contributes signedQty to delta. Short legs are negative. Excludes `lambda` (leverage is a ratio, not additive) — see each leg`s `greeks` for its lambda.

maxProfit.description: Maximum profit, or null when unbounded (see `unbounded.maxProfit`).

maxLoss.description: Maximum loss (most negative P&L), or null when unbounded.

riskRewardRatio.description: maxProfit / |maxLoss|; null when maxLoss is 0 or unbounded.

probabilityOfProfit.description: Lognormal probability of finishing in a profit zone; null unless sigma and tenor are known.

ivRmse.description: Aggregate IV RMSE across the options the fit was computed from. A calibration that does not converge returns a 422 `CALIBRATION_FAILED` rather than an `ivRmse` of 0 next to unfitted parameters.

nOptions.description: Number of usable observations admitted by the selected calibrator. This can differ from the submitted chain count: Heston requires a supplied IV in its accepted range; SABR, variance-gamma and jump-diffusion can derive IV from a usable option price; and local-vol/eSSVI deduplicates call/put observations at the same expiry and strike.

FitDiagnostics.description: Per-moneyness-bucket fit-quality diagnostics. Computed by re-pricing each market option with the calibrated parameters. Currently emitted for `model: "heston"` only; other models will gain support as their public price functions are exposed.

residuals.description: Per-option residuals (model price − market mid). Capped at 100, sorted by descending |residual| so the worst fits survive the cap.

bucketRmse.description: RMSE of price residuals within each moneyness bucket. Null when the bucket has no eligible options.

bucketCount.description: Number of options included in each moneyness bucket, mirrors `bucketRmse`.

worstFitOption.description: Single worst-fitting option in absolute residual terms. Null if no options were re-priceable.

moneyness.description: K / S at the time of calibration.

priceResidual.description: Model price − market mid (in price units, NOT IV units — aggregate `fitError.ivRmse` is the IV-space companion).

RegimeResponse.description: Latest market regime. Both `daily` and `intraday` are raw rows from the regime_daily / regime_intraday warehouse tables. Field set is owned by the data-pipeline team and may evolve over time — access defensively. Either field may be null when no row is available.

daily.description: Latest row from regime_daily for symbol=MARKET, scope=market, ordered by market_date desc. Null when no row exists.

intraday.description: Latest row from regime_intraday for symbol=MARKET, scope=market, ordered by (market_date, scan_time) desc. Null when no row exists.

MaxPainCurveRow.description: One per-strike row of the max-pain curve. Pain values are dollar-weighted aggregate OI × distance × multiplier.

SnapshotResponse.description: EOD options snapshot: spot, IV term structure, GEX/DEX/HV, max pain, plus opaque curve payloads consumed by the web app charts.

maxPainCurve.description: Max-pain curve series for the chart UI: per-strike rows of { strike, callPain, putPain, totalPain }.

chainData.description: Recent option chain rows; opaque payload

EodExposureResponse.description: Compact end-of-day dealer-positioning levels for one symbol, computed over a single 0-60 DTE universe so every field agrees: gamma magnet, gamma flip, call/put walls, dealer regime, net GEX/DEX, 30-day expected move, and the top strikes by gamma contribution. The window, units, and schemaVersion travel with every row. Returns 404 when no usable EOD option data exists for the symbol/date (e.g. thinly-traded names or futures symbols, which are not covered).

schemaVersion.description: Contract version; bumped on any breaking shape change.

date.description: EOD session the levels are computed from.

asOf.description: When the pipeline computed this row.

dteWindow.description: Expiration window every level is computed over.

netGex.description: Net dollar gamma exposure over the window (see units).

netDex.description: Net dollar delta exposure over the window (see units).

gammaMagnet.description: Strike with the largest absolute net gamma in the window.

dealerRegime.description: Sign of net gamma at spot over the window.

expectedMovePct30d.description: 30-day ATM-implied move as a decimal fraction.

topContributingStrikes.description: Strikes contributing most to net gamma, ordered by absolute gamma contribution.

topContributingStrikesLimit.description: Max number of rows returned in topContributingStrikes.

units.description: Plain-language units for the exposure and expected-move fields.

MetricsResponse.description: Per-symbol EOD metrics row. Sourced from option_ticker_snapshots.

IVSurfaceResponse.description: Strike × expiration grid of implied volatility for the symbol. Each row carries the smoothed value (`smv`), the call-side and put-side mid IVs, and a unified `iv` that falls back through smv → callIV → putIV. Any of the IV fields may be null when source data is missing.

ticker.description: Underlying symbol echoed from the request (uppercased).

date.description: Market date the surface snapshot applies to.

spotPrice.description: Spot price observed for this surface, in dollars.

expirations.description: Sorted list of distinct expiration dates present in `data`.

rowCount.description: Number of strike × expiration rows returned.

yte.description: Years to expiration as a decimal (calendar-day fraction).

iv.description: Unified IV — smv → callIV → putIV fallback. Null only if all three sources are missing.

atm_iv_7d.description: 7-day tenor ATM IV — closest persisted proxy to event-week vol around earnings.

workerPool.description: Current compute-worker capacity. Null means heavy computations have no worker pool and may use their documented fallback path.

redis.description: Redis connectivity. When Redis is down, the rate limiter and concurrency caps fall back to per-process memory and stop being global across replicas; response caching is bypassed.

rejections.description: Per-process refusal counters since startup. The path breakdown is capped; overflowed=true means totals remain complete but byBucket is partial.

CalibrationQuotaError.description: Returned by /v1/compute/calibrate when the user exceeds the per-day calibration cap. Separate from the general rate limit — calibrations are hard-capped because each run can consume 5-60 seconds of CPU.

limit.description: Hard cap for the scope (500 per day)

used.description: Number of successful calibrations the user has made in the scope window

resetsAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the quota window resets (UTC)

message.example: Heston sensitivity requires v0, kappa, theta, xi/volOfVol, and rho

missingFields.description: Fields that ticker resolution could not fill, present on RESOLUTION_FAILED responses

warnings.description: Non-fatal resolver warnings, present when ticker auto-fill ran

partialResolved.description: Resolved market inputs available before the semantic validation failure

error.example: No data found for this symbol
